# Reviewed residual surface: names that stay in generic Continuum code, why,
# and under which verdict.
#
# One entry per line:
#
#     verdict<TAB>expression<TAB>glob<TAB>reason
#
# A verdict is a *reason category*, not a synonym for "allowed":
#
#   release      GitHub requires this exact spelling to be literal. The only
#                instance is the Continuum release location and commit in a
#                `uses:`. It cannot be an expression, so the caller's pinned
#                ref is the only way to say it.
#   compat       Continuum's own migration surface: a token an *earlier*
#                Continuum release wrote into a consumer's issue bodies or
#                branch names. Reading it is how an in-flight migration
#                finishes; nothing routes on it.
#   provenance   A postmortem reference to the incident that produced the
#                code. It carries no operational value: no resolution reads
#                it, no dispatch matches on it, no configuration points at
#                it. It exists so the next reader knows why the code is
#                shaped the way it is.
#
# `python3 .github/scripts/consumer_boundary.py` fails when a recorded residual
# stops matching anything, so deleting a name from Continuum deletes its entry
# here too. A ledger that only grows is not a review.
#
# Sorted by path, then by expression.
provenance	kodmai	.github/scripts/agent_workspace.py	The module docstring cites the incident that produced the workspace publisher, including the pull-request body the failing step wrote. No code path reads the name; deleting it would delete the only record of why the recovery step refuses to trust the branch the model walked.
provenance	runtime[-_]lab	.github/scripts/agent_workspace.py	Same docstring, the other side of the same incident: the runner-only result that a crash would destroy. Carried so the section reads as one story rather than two half-explained ones.
provenance	runtime[-_]lab	.github/scripts/conflict_repair.py	The incident that made conflict repair a bounded operation on a finished change rather than a re-run of the source task, named at the four places the reasoning is load-bearing. The budget constant, the attempt cap, and the lock semantics all exist because of it.
